summary: Tests that a map location is accepted only when its place and region appear in the same source document.
purpose: Guards against map locations that the source never stated.
why: Likely reason: place names are easy to guess, so the grounding rule is tested directly.
how: 1. Build a sample sentence and candidate place. 2. Check that a grounded place passes. 3. Check that a changed place, a changed region, or a missing or different document fails.
inputs: A sample candidate location and sample source documents.
outputs: A pass or fail result for each test.
risks: Only the grounding rule is visible here. Other location tests are in a part not shown.
